Maria had always loved the smell of rain on dry earth. As a child she would race outside the moment thunder rolled across the valley, splashing barefoot through the puddles that formed along the gravel road. Her grandmother would scold her gently, wrapping a thick towel around her shoulders and pressing a steaming mug of cocoa into her cold hands. Years later, walking home through a sudden downpour in a city far from those hills, she felt the same wild joy rising in her chest, and she laughed out loud at nothing at all.
